provenance.source_location: mysql56-save_history.sql: INSERT INTO ... SELECT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
provenance.observed_pattern: A duplicate-key update uses LEAST/GREATEST with VALUES() to merge an incoming timestamp window into an existing row.
provenance.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reduced to one existing stream row, one duplicate source row, and one merge statement; the new-row insert path and aggregate checks are removed.

fixture_notes: The existing alpha window must expand to the earlier incoming start and later incoming end.
determinism_notes: All IDs and timestamps are fixed and the statement runs on one connection. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE stream_windows (stream_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, stream_key VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL UNIQUE, first_seen DATETIME NOT NULL, last_seen DATETIME NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE event_batch (event_id INT PRIMARY KEY, stream_key VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL, first_seen DATETIME NOT NULL, last_seen DATETIME NOT NULL)

steps.sql: INSERT INTO stream_windows (stream_key, first_seen, last_seen) SELECT stream_key, first_seen, last_seen FROM event_batch ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE first_seen = LEAST(stream_windows.first_seen, VALUES(first_seen)), last_seen = GREATEST(stream_windows.last_seen, VALUES(last_seen))

checks.sql: SELECT stream_id, stream_key, first_seen, last_seen FROM stream_windows ORDER BY stream_id
